+def _split_special(text, toks):
+    """
+    Same as re.split("(" + "|".join(map(re.escape, toks)) + ")", text), without
+    compiling a pattern: the leftmost occurrence of any token wins, and at the
+    same position the token listed first wins (regex alternation order).
+    """
+    if "" in toks:
+        # empty matches: leave those semantics to the regex engine
+        return re.split("(" + "|".join(re.escape(k) for k in toks) + ")", text)
+    find = text.find
+    nxt = [find(t) for t in toks]
+    n = len(toks)
+    parts = []
+    app = parts.append
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        best = -1
+        for i in range(n):
+            j = nxt[i]
+            if j >= 0 and (best < 0 or j < best):
+                best = j
+                bi = i
+        if best < 0:
+            break
+        t = toks[bi]
+        app(text[pos:best])
+        app(t)
+        pos = best + len(t)
+        for i in range(n):
+            j = nxt[i]
+            if 0 <= j < pos:
+                nxt[i] = find(toks[i], pos)
+    app(text[pos:])
+    return parts
+

I never ran a sandbox evaluation on either edit, so I have no measured results for them. The session stopped without submitting a candidate, which means nothing from this session goes to replay.

What I believe now is limited to what I read. regex.py is where most of the work happens. base.py holds the shared logic, and gpt4.py is a thin layer on top of them. I can't claim my edits help or hurt, because I never measured them.

Next session I should start by running lineage_bench.py on the unmodified code to get a baseline. Then I should re-apply the regex.py changes one at a time and evaluate each in the sandbox before deciding whether to submit.
